title: From Pitch to Profit: The Ultimate Playbook for App Funding

image.alt: From Pitch to Profit: The Ultimate Playbook for App Funding

body.text: Building a successful app takes more than a great idea. It takes money for design, development, testing and marketing. This playbook covers the main ways to fund an app and how to prepare to ask for it.
Estimate the cost of building your MVP, running it for 12 months and acquiring your first users. Add a buffer for the unexpected. Investors will ask for these numbers.

items: Bootstrapping: use your own savings and revenue to stay in full control.
Friends and family: quick and flexible, but keep terms in writing.
Angel investors: individuals who invest early and often bring experience.
Venture capital: larger amounts for fast-growing businesses, in exchange for equity.
Crowdfunding: raise money from many backers and test demand at the same time.
Grants and competitions: non-dilutive funding offered by programmes and incubators.

body.text: Show the problem, your solution, the size of the market, your traction and your team. A working prototype or early users make your case much stronger.
Investors back evidence. Launch a lean MVP, gather feedback and track the numbers that matter, such as sign-ups, retention and revenue.
Research who invests in your industry and stage. A warm introduction usually works better than a cold email.
Funding is a means, not a goal. Raise what you need to reach your next milestone, and use it wisely. We can help you scope and build an MVP that makes your pitch stronger.
